es: la donación de un monasterio; el dar / donar un monasterio. Los frutos de donar un monasterio, según el método de la enseñanza de los suttas, son: (1) *sītapaṭighāto* = el poder quitar el frío. (2) *uṇhapaṭighāto* el poder quitar el calor ardiente. (3) *ḍuṁsasamphassa-paṭighāto* el poder quitar el contacto de tábanos y mosquitos. (4) *makasasamphassa-paṭighāto* el poder quitar el contacto de las moscas. (5) *vātasamphassapaṭighāto* el poder quitar el contacto del viento. (6) *ātapasamphassapaṭighāto* = el poder quitar el contacto del calor del sol. (7) *sarīsapasamphassapaṭighāto* = el poder quitar el contacto de serpientes, escorpiones y piojos. (8) el poder quitar el peligro. (9) *paṭisallānārāmo* el deleitarse en el retiro, o bien el que la mente, apartándose de los diversos objetos hacia los que se dispersa, repose serenamente solo en el único objeto de *kammaṭṭhāna*, deleitándose y gozando en ello: así hay 9 clases. Según el método de la enseñanza del *vinaya*: (1) *sītapaṭighāto* = el poder quitar el frío. (2) *uṇhapaṭiyāto* = el poder quitar el calor ardiente. (3) *vāl̤amiga-paṭighāto* = el poder quitar las fieras, como ‹ခြေ›, tigres y demás. (4) *sarī-sapapaṭighāto* el poder quitar serpientes, escorpiones y piojos. (5) *makasapaṭighāto* = el poder quitar tábanos, mosquitos y moscas. (6) *sisirapaṭighāto* el poder quitar el viento que viene junto con las gotas de lluvia, o los vientos fríos. (7) *vuṭṭhipaṭighāto* = el poder quitar las gotas de lluvia que caen rectas porque no las azota el viento. (8) *yoravātapaṭighāto* el poder quitar los vientos violentos. (9) *yoraātapapaṭighāto* el poder quitar el calor intenso del sol. (10) *leṇaṁ* el ser un lugar de refugio. (11) *sukha* el poder morar felizmente. (12) *jhāyanaṁ* el poder entrar en *jhāna*. (13) *vipassanā* el poder contemplar con *vipassanā*. (14) *annapānavatthasenāsanalābho* el obtener comida, bebida, hábitos y lecho y asiento. (15) *dhammassavanaṁ* el poder escuchar la Enseñanza. (16) *dhammāvabodho* el llegar a conocer la Enseñanza penetrándola. (17) *parinibbānaṁ* el llegar a entrar en el *parinibbāna*: así hay 17 clases. (De los frutos así expuestos, los 9 frutos de la enseñanza de los suttas y los 14 frutos del 1 al 14 de la enseñanza del *vinaya* son frutos que obtiene la persona que recibe la donación, mientras que los 3 frutos hasta el 17 son frutos que obtiene la persona que da la donación. Aunque así se distinguen frutos que obtiene quien recibe y frutos que obtiene quien da, de acuerdo con [la cita] 320, también quienes dan pueden obtener todos los frutos que obtienen quienes reciben.) Además, se enseña que, por el poder de donar un monasterio, al tomar *paṭisandhi* en el vientre materno no hay estrechez ni apretura, sino que es como morar en una estancia de 12 codos; que donar un monasterio *cātuddisa* *saṁghika* tiene un fruto mayor que ofrecer comida de limosna al *saṅgha* presidido por el Buddha; que por donar un monasterio se obtienen 2 frutos: (1) que los donantes del monasterio pueden liberarse y salir de los sufrimientos del tomar *paṭisandhi*, del envejecer y del morir; (2) que, por haber un monasterio, para las *bhikkhunī* se hace evidente la señal / marca «este lugar es el lugar de los monjes», y que quienes desean ver a los monjes pueden verlos con facilidad; que por donar un monasterio se nace en los mundos de los *deva* 1, 00 [sic], 1000 y 10000 veces, y las veces que se nace en el mundo humano no pueden decirse, y que al nacer en el mundo humano o en el de los *deva* se nace solo como ser humano o *deva* de gran poder; que quien dona un monasterio, porque impide sufrimientos como el frío, el calor ardiente, el viento, el calor del sol, los tábanos, los mosquitos, la lluvia, las serpientes, los escorpiones, los piojos, las fieras y demás, goza de felicidad en la existencia siguiente, y que tras gozar en las existencias de *sugati* de riquezas y bienes deleitables, más tarde goza de la felicidad sumamente apacible del Nibbāna; que para la persona que dona un monasterio los estados sanos crecen día y noche, en todo momento; que quien dona un monasterio es llamado dador de vida, belleza, felicidad, fuerza y excelente conocimiento y *paññā*; que del fruto de un cobertizo techado con hojas o de un pabellón techado con ramas, construido en buena tierra con un objeto (receptor) fuerte, quien dona un monasterio no puede delimitar diciendo «es así de grande». Así se enseñó de diversas maneras el fruto de donar un monasterio. Los frutos aquí expuestos no son completos; son solo una breve mención. El fruto completo de donar un monasterio no pueden enseñarlo personas distintas del Buddha; incluso el Buddha tuvo que enseñar el fruto de donar un monasterio durante mucho tiempo, cerca de una vigilia y media o dos vigilias de la noche (la primera vigilia y la vigilia media).
en: the donation of a monastery; the giving / donating of a monastery. The fruits of donating a monastery, according to the method of the Suttanta teaching, are: (1) *sītapaṭighāto* = being able to ward off the cold. (2) *uṇhapaṭighāto* being able to ward off burning heat. (3) *ḍuṁsasamphassa-paṭighāto* being able to ward off the contact of gadflies and mosquitoes. (4) *makasasamphassa-paṭighāto* being able to ward off the contact of flies. (5) *vātasamphassapaṭighāto* being able to ward off the contact of the wind. (6) *ātapasamphassapaṭighāto* = being able to ward off the contact of the sun's heat. (7) *sarīsapasamphassapaṭighāto* = being able to ward off the contact of snakes, scorpions and lice. (8) being able to ward off danger. (9) *paṭisallānārāmo* delighting in seclusion, or the mind, turning back from the various objects to which it strays, resting calmly on the single object of *kammaṭṭhāna* alone, delighting and rejoicing in it: thus there are 9 kinds. According to the method of the *vinaya* teaching: (1) *sītapaṭighāto* = being able to ward off the cold. (2) *uṇhapaṭiyāto* = being able to ward off burning heat. (3) *vāl̤amiga-paṭighāto* = being able to ward off wild beasts such as ‹ခြေ›, tigers and so on. (4) *sarī-sapapaṭighāto* being able to ward off snakes, scorpions and lice. (5) *makasapaṭighāto* = being able to ward off gadflies, mosquitoes and flies. (6) *sisirapaṭighāto* being able to ward off the wind that comes with raindrops, or cold winds. (7) *vuṭṭhipaṭighāto* = being able to ward off raindrops that fall straight down because the wind does not drive them. (8) *yoravātapaṭighāto* being able to ward off violent winds. (9) *yoraātapapaṭighāto* being able to ward off the fierce heat of the sun. (10) *leṇaṁ* being a place of refuge. (11) *sukha* being able to dwell happily. (12) *jhāyanaṁ* being able to enter *jhāna*. (13) *vipassanā* being able to contemplate with *vipassanā*. (14) *annapānavatthasenāsanalābho* obtaining food, drink, robes, and bed and seat. (15) *dhammassavanaṁ* being able to hear the Teaching. (16) *dhammāvabodho* coming to know the Teaching by penetrating it. (17) *parinibbānaṁ* coming to enter *parinibbāna*: thus there are 17 kinds. (Of the fruits thus stated, the 9 fruits of the Suttanta teaching and the 14 fruits, 1 to 14, of the *vinaya* teaching are fruits obtained by the person who receives the gift, while the 3 fruits up to 17 are fruits obtained by the person who gives it. Although they are thus distinguished as fruits obtained by the recipient and fruits obtained by the giver, in accordance with [the quotation at] 320 the givers too can obtain all the fruits that the recipients obtain.) Besides this, it is taught that, through the power of donating a monastery, when one takes *paṭisandhi* in the mother's womb there is no narrowness or cramping, but it is as if one dwelt in a chamber of 12 cubits; that donating a *cātuddisa* *saṁghika* monastery has greater fruit than offering almsfood to the *saṅgha* headed by the Buddha; that by donating a monastery one obtains 2 fruits: (1) the donors of the monastery can be freed from and escape the sufferings of taking *paṭisandhi*, of ageing and of dying; (2) because there is a monastery, the sign / mark 'this place is the place of the monks' becomes evident to the *bhikkhunī*s, and those who wish to see the monks can see them easily; that by donating a monastery one is born in the *deva* worlds 1, 00 [sic], 1000 and 10000 times, while the times one is born in the human world cannot be told, and that when born in the human or *deva* worlds one is born only as a human being or *deva* of great power; that one who donates a monastery, because it keeps off hardships such as cold, burning heat, wind, the sun's heat, gadflies, mosquitoes, rain, snakes, scorpions, lice, wild beasts and so on, enjoys happiness in the next existence, and having enjoyed delightful wealth and riches in the existences of *sugati*, later enjoys the most peaceful happiness of Nibbāna; that for the person who donates a monastery wholesome states grow day and night, at all times; that one who donates a monastery is called a giver of life, beauty, happiness, strength and excellent knowledge and *paññā*; that even of a rest-house roofed with leaves or a pavilion roofed with branches, built on good ground with a strong object (recipient), the one who donates a monastery cannot delimit the fruit, saying 'it is this much'. Thus the fruit of donating a monastery was taught in various ways. The fruits stated here are not complete; they are only a brief mention. The complete fruit of donating a monastery persons other than the Buddha are unable to teach; even the Buddha had to teach the fruit of donating a monastery at length, for about one and a half to two watches of the night (the first watch and the middle watch).

es: el defecto de un monasterio. (Los 18 defectos de un monasterio son: (1) *mahatta* = el ser un monasterio demasiado grande. (2) *navatta* = el ser un monasterio nuevo. (3) *jiṇṇatta* el ser un monasterio podrido, ruinoso y viejo. (4) *panthanissitatta* = el ser un monasterio que está junto a un camino. (5) *soṇḍī* el ser un monasterio que tiene un estanque de roca. (6) *paṇṇa* = el ser un monasterio que tiene un huerto de hortalizas. (7) *puppha* = el ser un monasterio que tiene un jardín de flores. (8) *phala* = el ser un monasterio que tiene un huerto de frutales. (9) *patthanīyatā* el ser un monasterio deseado y alabado por la gente. (10) *nagarasannissitatā* el ser un monasterio que está junto a una ciudad o una aldea. (11) *dārusannissitatā* el ser un monasterio que está junto a un bosque de leña o un bosque de árboles. (12) *khettasannissitatā* = el ser un monasterio que está junto a arrozales. (13) = el ser un monasterio donde hay personas hostiles que no están de acuerdo. (14) *paṭṭanasannissitatā* el ser un monasterio que está junto a un embarcadero (un fondeadero de barcas, un puerto de barcos). (15) el ser un monasterio que está junto a (la región del borde del país, cerca de sus confines). (16) *rajjasīmasannissitatā* = el ser un monasterio que está junto a la frontera, el límite del reino. (17) *asappāyatā* = el ser un monasterio inadecuado (ya sea por la concurrencia de objetos incompatibles, ya por estar ocupado por *yakkha*). (18) = el no conseguir buenos amigos.)
en: the fault of a monastery. (The 18 faults of a monastery are: (1) *mahatta* = being a monastery that is too large. (2) *navatta* = being a new monastery. (3) *jiṇṇatta* being a monastery that is rotten, decayed and old. (4) *panthanissitatta* = being a monastery beside a road. (5) *soṇḍī* being a monastery that has a rock pool. (6) *paṇṇa* = being a monastery that has a vegetable garden. (7) *puppha* = being a monastery that has a flower garden. (8) *phala* = being a monastery that has a fruit orchard. (9) *patthanīyatā* being a monastery longed for and praised by people. (10) *nagarasannissitatā* being a monastery near a town or village. (11) *dārusannissitatā* being a monastery near a firewood forest or a timber forest. (12) *khettasannissitatā* = being a monastery near rice fields. (13) = being a monastery where there are hostile persons who do not agree. (14) *paṭṭanasannissitatā* being a monastery near a landing place (a boat landing, a ship's harbour). (15) being a monastery near (the region at the edge of the country, near its borders). (16) *rajjasīmasannissitatā* = being a monastery near the frontier, the boundary of the kingdom. (17) *asappāyatā* = being an unsuitable monastery (whether through the meeting of incompatible objects, or through being taken over by *yakkha*s). (18) = not obtaining good friends.)

(d) el deseo, *chanda*. (3) el sufrir fatiga / hambre / sed. (4) la palabra *vihiṁsā*. (La *vihiṁsā* tiene como característica atormentar a otros seres; (o bien) tiene como característica existir como lo opuesto de la *karuṇā*. Tiene como función producir sobresalto en el *santāna* de otro; (o bien) tiene como función destruir la *karuṇā* en el propio *santāna*; se manifiesta como causa de sufrimiento; tiene como causa próxima la ira. La *vihiṁsā* se llama el enemigo lejano del *karuṇābrahmavihāra*. Para eliminar la *vihiṁsā* se debe cultivar la *avihiṁsā* = la *karuṇābhāvanā*.) Véanse también [[vihiṁsādhātu]], [[vihiṁsātakka]]. Véase también [[vihiṁsūparati]].
en: (1) the tormenting / oppressing / causing to suffer. (2) the cause of tormenting / oppressing / causing to suffer: (a) *dosa*, the *dosamūlacittuppāda*. (b) *vitakka*, thought. (c) *cetanā*. (d) desire, *chanda*. (3) the suffering of weariness / hunger / thirst. (4) the word *vihiṁsā*. (*vihiṁsā* has the characteristic of tormenting other beings; (or) has the characteristic of occurring as the opposite of *karuṇā*. It has the function of producing alarm in another's *santāna*; (or) has the function of destroying *karuṇā* in one's own *santāna*; it is manifested as the cause of suffering; its proximate cause is anger. *vihiṁsā* is called the far enemy of the *karuṇābrahmavihāra*. To eliminate *vihiṁsā* one should cultivate *avihiṁsā* = *karuṇābhāvanā*.) See also [[vihiṁsādhātu]], [[vihiṁsātakka]]. See also [[vihiṁsūparati]].

es: el *thera* *vītasoka*. (Este *thera*, en tiempos del Buddha *siddhattha*, nació en una familia de brahmanes y llegó a dominar las ciencias y las artes que conviene y corresponde aprender a los brahmanes. Después, abandonando los *kāmaguṇa*, se hizo ermitaño y, mientras moraba en el bosque rodeado de muchos ermitaños, oyó que había aparecido un Buddha; gozoso y alegre, se puso en camino con una gran asamblea para ver al Buddha, pero en el camino, afligido por una enfermedad, murió con la *saññā* puesta en el Buddha y, tras errar por los mundos de los *deva* y de los humanos, más de 200 años después de la aparición del Buddha *gotama* nació como hermano menor del gran rey *dhammāsoka* y recibió el nombre de «*vītasoka*». Este príncipe *vītasoka* dominó por completo las ciencias y las artes que conviene y corresponde aprender a los príncipes y, siendo aún laico, aprendió del *thera* *giridatta* los *piṭaka* de los suttas y del *abhidhamma*; al ver el arrugarse de la piel, el encanecer del cabello y demás, sintió *saṁvega* por el Dhamma y se esforzó en la práctica; al instante se estableció como *sotāpanna*, se hizo monje junto al mismo *thera* *giridatta* y al poco tiempo alcanzó el estado de *arahant*, con los *āsava* agotados.)
en: the *thera* *vītasoka*. (This *thera*, in the time of the Buddha *siddhattha*, was born in a brahmin family and mastered the sciences and arts that brahmins ought and are fit to learn. Then, abandoning the *kāmaguṇa*s, he became a hermit and, while dwelling in the forest surrounded by many hermits, he heard that a Buddha had appeared; glad and joyful, he set out with a large assembly to see the Buddha, but on the way, afflicted by illness, he died with his *saññā* set on the Buddha and, after faring through the worlds of *deva*s and humans, more than 200 years after the appearance of the Buddha *gotama* he was born as the younger brother of the great king *dhammāsoka* and was named '*vītasoka*'. This prince *vītasoka* fully mastered the sciences and arts that princes ought and are fit to learn and, while still a layman, learnt the Sutta and *abhidhamma* *piṭaka*s from the *thera* *giridatta*; seeing the wrinkling of the skin, the greying of the hair and so on, he felt *saṁvega* for the Dhamma and strove in practice; at once he became established as a *sotāpanna*, became a monk under that same *thera* *giridatta*, and before long reached the state of *arahant*, with the *āsava*s exhausted.)

es: (1) camino, ruta; camino / ruta / trayecto; caminos en general; camino secundario, calle dentro de la ciudad o de la aldea; callejón; sendero; camino corriente. (2) camino principal; calle principal, calle ancha / grande. (3) (por donde se desplazan la luna, el sol, las constelaciones, las estrellas y demás) camino. El camino de los planetas; la ruta del cielo. (Los caminos por donde se desplazan la luna y el sol son de tres clases: (1) *ajavīthi* = el camino de la luna y el sol semejante a una cabra, o el camino de la luna y el sol en la estación propia de la cabra; (2) *nāgavīthi* = el camino de la luna y el sol semejante a un elefante, o el camino de la luna y el sol en la estación propia del elefante; (3) *govīthi* = el camino de la luna y el sol semejante a un buey, o el camino de la luna y el sol en la estación propia del buey. Entradas *ajavīthi*, *nāgavīthi*, *govīthi*.) (4) el camino que es el *ariyamagga*. (5) (a) el camino / la vía establecida / el camino recto que es el *kammaṭṭhāna*. (b) el camino / la vía establecida / el camino recto que es la *bhāvanā*. (c) el camino / la vía establecida / el camino recto que es la *vipassanā*. Véase también [[vipassanāvīthi]]. (6) el camino que es la *saccā* / de las *saccā* (el objeto verdadero llamado *diṭṭha*, *suta*, *muta*, *viññāta*, *adiṭṭha*, *asuta*, *amuta*, *aviññāta*). (7) (a) sucesión. (b) la sucesión / serie de las mentes; la *vīthi* (que comienza por la *cakkhudvāravīthi*). (Véanse [[vīthicitta]] y demás entradas.) La sucesión de mentes que comienza por *atītabhavaṅga*, *bhavaṅgacalana*, *bhavaṅgupaccheda*, *pañcadvārāvajjana*, *cakkhuviññāṇa*, *sampaṭicchana*, siete veces *javana* y dos veces *tadārammaṇa*, de acuerdo con la definición verbal «…», así como el camino por donde van los seres avanza sin saltarse la sucesión de las aldeas, se llama *vīthi* porque se parece a un recorrido, en cuanto una mente no salta sobre otra, sino que surge solo en su orden. Esa *vīthi* es de 2 clases: *pañcadvāravīthi* y *manodvāravīthi*. De ellas, la *pañcadvāravīthi* es de 5 clases: *cakkhudvāravīthi*, *sotadvāravīthi*, *ghānadvāravīthi*, *jivhādvāravīthi* y *kāyadvāravīthi*. De ellas, la *cakkhudvāravīthi* es de 2 clases: la *vīthi* en que no se produce *āgantukabhavaṅga* y la *vīthi* en que se produce *āgantukabhavaṅga*. De ellas, la *vīthi* en que no se produce *āgantukabhavaṅga* es de 4 clases: *atimahantārammaṇavīthi*, *mahantārammaṇavīthi*, *parittārammaṇavīthi* y *atiparittārammaṇavīthi*. De ellas, la *atimahantārammaṇavīthi* es de 2 clases: *tadārammaṇavāra* y *javanavāra*. La *mahantārammaṇavīthi* es de 2 clases: la *vīthi* en que el *atītabhavaṅga* ha pasado 2 veces y la *vīthi* en que ha pasado 3 veces. La *parittārammaṇavīthi* es de 6 clases: desde la *vīthi* en que el *atītabhavaṅga* ha pasado 4 veces hasta la *vīthi* en que ha pasado 9 veces. La *atiparittārammaṇavīthi*: desde la *vīthi* en que el *atītabhavaṅga* ha pasado 10 veces hasta la *vīthi* en que ha pasado 15 veces […]. Las *cakkhudvāravīthi* en que no se produce *āgantukabhavaṅga* suman 16. La *vīthi* en que se produce *āgantukabhavaṅga* es de 2 clases: *atimahantārammaṇavīthi* y *mahantārammaṇavīthi*. De ellas, la *atimahantārammaṇavīthi* es de una sola clase: la *vīthi* en que el *atītabhavaṅga* ha pasado 1 vez. La *mahantārammaṇavīthi* es de 2 clases: la *vīthi* en que el *atītabhavaṅga* ha pasado 2 veces y la *vīthi* en que ha pasado 3 veces. Así, las *cakkhudvāravīthi* en que se produce *āgantukabhavaṅga* suman 3. Sumadas las 2, la *vīthi* en que no se produce *āgantukabhavaṅga* y la *vīthi* en que se produce, las *cakkhudvāravīthi* suman (16 + 3) 19. Del mismo modo, como la *sotadvāravīthi*, la *ghānadvāravīthi*, la *jivhādvāravīthi* y la *kāyadvāravīthi* son también de 19 clases cada una, las *pañcadvāravīthi* suman (19 × 5) 95. Por *bhūmi*: de esas 5 clases de *vīthi*, estas 65 *vīthi* —la *cakkhudvāra* *atimahantārammaṇavīthi* *tadārammaṇavāra* (1), las [*cakkhudvāravīthi*] en que se produce *āgantukabhavaṅga* (3), la *sotadvāra* *atimahantārammaṇavīthi* *tadārammaṇavāra* (1), las *sotadvāravīthi* en que se produce *āgantukabhavaṅga* (3), las *ghānadvāravīthi* (19), las *jivhādvāravīthi* (19) y las *kāyadvāravīthi* (19)— surgen solo en las 11 *bhūmi* *kāma*. Las 30 restantes surgen en las 26 *bhūmi* *pañcavokāra*. Por persona: las 95 surgen en los 4 *puthujjana* y los 4 *phalaṭṭha*, 8 personas en total. La *manodvāravīthi* es a su vez de 2 clases: *kāmajavanavīthi* y *appanājavanavīthi*. De ellas, la *kāmajavanavīthi* es de 9 clases: en el objeto que es los 22 *rūpa* presentes capaces de durar diecisiete [momentos], excluidas las dos *viññatti* y los [4] *lakkhaṇarūpa*, las *vīthi* *vibhūtārammaṇa* (5) y [*avibhūtārammaṇa*] (2); en el objeto que es los *rūpa* restantes, incapaces de durar diecisiete [momentos], el *nāma* y la *paññatti*, las *vīthi* *vibhūtārammaṇa* (1) y [*avibhūtārammaṇa*] (1). Por *bhūmi*: las 6 *vīthi* *vibhūtārammaṇa* surgen solo en las [11] *bhūmi* *kāma*; las 3 *vīthi* *avibhūtārammaṇa* surgen en las 30 *bhūmi*, excluida la *asaññasatta*. Por persona: las 9 *manodvāravīthi* surgen en estas 8: los 4 *puthujjana* y los 4 *phalaṭṭha*. La *vīthi* del sueño (o …): de acuerdo con «…» y «…», cuando en un sueño es como si uno viera, como si oyera, tomando por objeto uno cualquiera, no advertido, de los 6 objetos, surgen *bhavaṅgacalana*, *bhavaṅgupaccheda* y *manodvārāvajjana*, [y el *javana*] 2 o 3 veces, y después el *bhavaṅga* cuanto corresponda: hay todavía esta clase más, la *vīthi* *abyākata* *manodvāra* *avibhūtārammaṇa*. Contando también esa *vīthi*, las *vīthi* *manodvāra* de *kāmajavana* suman 10. Por *bhūmi*, la *vīthi* del sueño surge solo en la *bhūmi* humana; por persona, la *vīthi* del sueño surge solo en estas 7: los 4 *puthujjana*, el *sotāpattiphalaṭṭha*, el *sakadāgāmiphalaṭṭha* y el *anāgāmiphalaṭṭha*. La *maraṇāsannavīthi* queda también incluida, según corresponda, en estas mismas *vīthi* *kāmāvacara*. Por eso esa *maraṇāsannavīthi* es de 2 clases: *pañcadvāravīthi* y *manodvāravīthi*. De ellas, la *pañcadvāravīthi* es de 5 clases: *cakkhudvāravīthi*, *sotadvāravīthi*, *ghānadvāravīthi*, *jivhādvāravīthi* y *kāyadvāravīthi*. De ellas, la *cakkhudvāravīthi* es de 4 clases: la *vīthi* en que la *cuti* se produce después del *javana*; la *vīthi* en que la *cuti* se produce después del *javana* y el *bhavaṅga*; la *vīthi* en que la *cuti* se produce después del *tadārammaṇa*; y la *vīthi* en que la *cuti* se produce después del *tadārammaṇa* y el *bhavaṅga*. Del mismo modo, como la *sotadvāravīthi*, la *ghānadvāravīthi*, la *jivhādvāravīthi* y la *kāyadvāravīthi* son también de 4 clases cada una, las *pañcadvāra* *maraṇāsannavīthi* suman (5 × 4) 20. (Nota: en ‹ဝီထိလက်ရိုး› y en el *paramatthasarūpabhedanī* se dice que estas 20 *pañcadvāra* *maraṇāsannavīthi* surgen solo en los 4 *puthujjana* y los 2 *phalaṭṭha* inferiores que, muriendo en la *bhūmi* *kāma*, han de renacer en la *bhūmi* *kāma*. En la *bhāsāṭīkā*, en cambio, se dice que, de esas 20 *vīthi*, estas 4 —la *cakkhudvāravīthi* y la *sotadvāravīthi* en que la *cuti* se produce después del *javana*, y la *cakkhudvāravīthi* y la *sotadvāravīthi* en que la *cuti* se produce después del *javana* y el *bhavaṅga*— surgen [en quienes], muriendo en las 10 *bhūmi* hasta *vehapphala*, [renacen] en la *bhūmi* *kāmasugati*.) La *manodvāravīthi* es a su vez de 2 clases: la *maraṇāsannavīthi* de los *puthujjana* y los *sekkha*, y la *maraṇāsannavīthi* de los *arahant*. De ellas, la *maraṇāsannavīthi* de los *puthujjana* y los *sekkha* es de 9 clases: (1) la *vīthi* de estos 6: los 4 *puthujjana* y los 2 *phalaṭṭha* inferiores que, muriendo en las 11 *bhūmi* *kāma*, han de renacer en las 11 *bhūmi* *kāma*; (2) la *vīthi* de estos 4: el *puthujjana* *tihetuka* y los 3 *phalaṭṭha* inferiores que, muriendo en las 7 *bhūmi* *kāmasugati*, han de renacer en las 15 *bhūmi* *rūpa*, excluida la *asaññasatta*; (3) la *vīthi* del *puthujjana* *tihetuka* que, muriendo en las 7 *bhūmi* *kāmasugati*, ha de renacer en la *bhūmi* *asaññasatta*; (4) la *vīthi* de estos 4: el *puthujjana* *tihetuka* y los 3 *phalaṭṭha* inferiores que, muriendo en las 7 *bhūmi* *kāmasugati*, han de renacer en las 4 *bhūmi* *arūpa*; (5) la *vīthi* de estos 4: el *puthujjana* *tihetuka* y los 3 *phalaṭṭha* inferiores que, muriendo en las 15 *bhūmi* *rūpa*, excluida la *asaññasatta*, han de renacer en las 15 *bhūmi* *rūpa*, excluida la *asaññasatta*; (6) la *vīthi* del *puthujjana* *tihetuka* que, muriendo en las 10 *bhūmi* *rūpa* hasta *vehapphala*, ha de renacer en las 7 *bhūmi* *kāmasugati*; (7) la *vīthi* de estos 4: el *puthujjana* *tihetuka* y los 3 *phalaṭṭha* inferiores que, muriendo en las 10 *bhūmi* *rūpa* hasta *vehapphala*, han de renacer en las 4 *bhūmi* *arūpa*; (8) la *vīthi* de estos 4: el *puthujjana* *tihetuka* y los 3 *phalaṭṭha* inferiores que, muriendo en las 4 *bhūmi* *arūpa*, han de renacer en las 4 *bhūmi* *arūpa*; (9) la *vīthi* del *puthujjana* *tihetuka* que, muriendo en las 4 *bhūmi* *arūpa*, ha de renacer en las 7 *bhūmi* *kāmasugati*. De ellas, la *vīthi* de los 6 —los 4 *puthujjana* y los 2 *phalaṭṭha* inferiores que, muriendo en las 11 *bhūmi* *kāma*, han de renacer en las 11 *bhūmi*— es de 4 clases: la *vīthi* (1) después del *javana*, (2) después del *javana* y el *bhavaṅga*, (3) después del *tadārammaṇa*, (4) después del *tadārammaṇa* y el *bhavaṅga*. De las 8 *vīthi* restantes, cada una se divide en 2: (1) la *vīthi* en que la *cuti* se produce después del *javana*, (2) la *vīthi* en que la *cuti* se produce después del *javana* y el *bhavaṅga*; por eso las *manodvāra* *maraṇāsannavīthi* de los *puthujjana* y los *sekkha* suman (4 + 16) = 20. La *maraṇāsannavīthi* de los *arahant* es a su vez de 3 clases: (1) la *vīthi* de los *arahant* habitantes de la *bhūmi* *kāma*, (2) la *vīthi* de los *arahant* habitantes de la *bhūmi* *rūpa*, (3) la *vīthi* de los *arahant* habitantes de la *bhūmi* *arūpa*. De ellas, la *vīthi* de los *arahant* habitantes de la *bhūmi* *kāma* es de 4 clases: la *vīthi* en que la *cuti* se produce (1) después del *javana*, (2) después del *javana* y el *bhavaṅga*, (3) después del *tadārammaṇa*, (4) después del *tadārammaṇa* y el *bhavaṅga*. De las 2 *vīthi* restantes, cada una se divide en 2: (1) la *vīthi* en que la *cuti* se produce después del *javana*, (2) la *vīthi* en que la *cuti* se produce después del *javana* y el *bhavaṅga*; por eso las *manodvāra* *maraṇāsannavīthi* de los *arahant* suman (4 + 4) 8. Así, sumadas las 2, la *maraṇāsannavīthi* de los *puthujjana* y los *sekkha* y la de los *arahant*, las *manodvāra* *maraṇāsannavīthi* suman (20 + 8) = 28. Sumadas las 2, las *pañcadvāra* *maraṇāsannavīthi* y las *manodvāra* *maraṇāsannavīthi*, las *maraṇāsannavīthi* suman (20 + 28) = 48. Nota: la *vīthi* del *puthujjana* *ahetuka* de destino feliz que, muriendo en la *bhūmi* *asaññasatta*, ha de renacer en las 7 *bhūmi* *kāmasugati* se ha dejado fuera porque hay *nāma* solo en la nueva existencia y no hay *nāma* en la existencia anterior. Téngase presente que, contándola también, las *maraṇāsannavīthi* suman 49. «*appanāvīthi*». La *appanāvīthi* es a su vez de 5 clases: *jhānavīthi*, *maggavīthi*, *phalasamāpattivīthi*, *abhiññāvīthi* y *nirodhasamāpattivīthi*. De ellas, la *jhānavīthi* es de 2 clases: *ādikammikavīthi* y *samāpattivīthi*. De ellas, la *ādikammikavīthi* es de 9 clases: (1) *rūpapaṭhamajjhānavīthi*, (2) *rūpadutiyajjhānavīthi*, (3) *rūpatatiyajjhānavīthi*, (4) *rūpacatutthajjhānavīthi*, (5) […], (6) […], (7) *viññāṇañcāyatanajjhānavīthi*, (8) *ākiñcaññāyatanajjhānavīthi*, (9) *nevasaññānāsaññāyatanajjhānavīthi*. De ellas, cada una se divide en 2, como sana y *kiriya*; por eso, tomando esos 9 *jhāna* y multiplicando por 2, las *vīthi* *ādikammika* de *jhāna* suman (9 × 2) 18. De esas 18, cada una se divide en 2, la *vīthi* de la persona aguda y la *vīthi* de la persona torpe; por eso, tomando esas 18 y multiplicando por 2, las *vīthi* *ādikammika* de *jhāna* suman (18 × 2) 36. Del mismo modo, como la *samāpattivīthi* es también de 36 clases, sumadas las 2, las *jhānavīthi* suman (36 × 2) 72. (Aquí quedan incluidas 8 *vīthi* del primer *jhāna*, 8 *vīthi* del segundo *jhāna*, 8 del tercer *jhāna*, 8 *vīthi* del [cuarto] *jhāna* y 40 *vīthi* del quinto *jhāna*.) Por *bhūmi*: de esas 72 *jhānavīthi*, las 4 *paṭhamajjhānaādikammikavīthi* surgen solo en las 7 *bhūmi* *kāmasugati*. Las 4 *dutiyajjhānaādikammikavīthi* y las 4 *tatiyajjhānaādikammikavīthi* surgen solo en las 7 *bhūmi* *kāmasugati* y en las 3 *bhūmi* del primer *jhāna*. Las 4 *catutthajjhānaādikammikavīthi* surgen solo en las 7 *bhūmi* *kāmasugati*, en las 3 *bhūmi* del primer *jhāna* y en las 3 *bhūmi* del segundo *jhāna*. La *pañcamajjhānaādikammikavīthi* surge solo en las 7 *bhūmi* *kāmasugati*, en las 3 *bhūmi* del primer *jhāna*, en las 3 *bhūmi* del segundo *jhāna* y en las 3 *bhūmi* del tercer *jhāna*. Las 4 *ākāsānañcāyatanaādikammikavīthi* surgen solo en las 7 *bhūmi* *kāmasugati* y en las [15] *bhūmi* *rūpa*, excluida la *asaññasatta*. […] las 4 surgen solo en las 7 *bhūmi* *kāmasugati*, en las 15 *bhūmi* *rūpa*, excluida la *asaññasatta*, y en la *bhūmi* *ākāsānañcāyatana*. […] las 4 surgen solo en las [7] *bhūmi* *kāmasugati*, en las [15] *bhūmi* *rūpa*, excluida la *asaññasatta*, en la *bhūmi* *ākāsānañcāyatana* y en la *bhūmi* *viññāṇañcāyatana*. […] las 4 surgen solo en las 7 *bhūmi* *kāmasugati*, en las [15] *bhūmi*, excluida la *asaññasatta*, en la *bhūmi* *ākāsānañcāyatana*, en la *bhūmi* *viññāṇañcāyatana* y en la *bhūmi* *ākiñcaññāyatana*. En cuanto a la *samāpattivīthi*, en las [7] *bhūmi* *kāmasugati* y en las [15] *bhūmi* *rūpa*, excluida la *asaññasatta*, surgen las 36 *samāpattivīthi* enteras. En la *bhūmi* *ākāsānañcāyatana* surgen solo 16. En la *bhūmi* *viññāṇañcāyatana* surgen solo 4, 4 y 4, en total 12 *samāpattivīthi*. En la *bhūmi* *ākiñcaññāyatana* surgen solo 4 y 4, en total 8 *samāpattivīthi*. En la *bhūmi* *nevasaññānāsaññāyatana* surgen solo 4. Por persona: las 72 *jhānavīthi* surgen en estas 5 personas: la persona *puthujjana* *tihetuka* y las 4 personas *phalaṭṭha*. «*paccavekkhaṇāvīthi*». Al final de esas *jhānavīthi* surgen además, según corresponda, con un *bhavaṅga* intermedio, *paccavekkhaṇāvīthi* que reflexionan sobre los factores del *jhāna*. Como esas *paccavekkhaṇāvīthi* se obtienen una *vīthi* por cada factor del *jhāna*, después de las 8 *vīthi* del primer *jhāna* hay (8 × 5) = 40; después de las 8 *vīthi* del segundo *jhāna*, (8 × 4) = 32; después de las 8 *vīthi* del tercer *jhāna*, (8 × 3) 24; después de las 8 *vīthi* del cuarto *jhāna*, (8 × 2) = 16; después de las 40 *vīthi* del quinto *jhāna*, (40 × 2) = 80: las *paccavekkhaṇāvīthi* suman 192. Por *bhūmi* y por persona, las *paccavekkhaṇāvīthi* surgen igual que las *jhānavīthi* correspondientes. Estas *paccavekkhaṇāvīthi* quedan incluidas, según corresponda, en las mismas *vīthi* *kāma* *manodvāra* antes expuestas. Nota: en ‹ဝီထိလက်ရိုး› y en ‹ဝီထိပုံ› se habla de la *paccavekkhaṇāvīthi* solo inmediatamente después de la *vīthi* *ādikammika* de *jhāna*; en el *paramatthasarūpabhedanī* y en la *bhāsāṭīkā*, en cambio, se habla de la *paccavekkhaṇāvīthi* también inmediatamente después de la *samāpattivīthi*. «*maggavīthi*». La *maggavīthi* es de 4 clases: *sotāpattimaggavīthi*, *sakadāgāmimaggavīthi*, *anāgāmimaggavīthi* y *arahattamaggavīthi*. De ellas, la *sotāpattimaggavīthi* es de 5 clases: *paṭhamajjhānavīthi*, *dutiyajjhānavīthi*, *tatiyajjhānavīthi*, *catutthajjhānavīthi* y *pañcamajjhānavīthi*. De ellas, cada una se divide en 2, la *vīthi* de la persona aguda y la *vīthi* de la persona torpe; por eso, tomando las 5 que se dividen en virtud del *jhāna* y multiplicando por 2, resultan 10. De esas 10 *sotāpattimaggavīthi*, cada una se divide en 3, en virtud del *pādakajjhāna*, el *sammasitajjhāna* y el *puggalajjhāsaya*; por eso, tomando las 10 y multiplicando por 3, las *sotāpattimaggavīthi* suman 30. Del mismo modo, como los 3 *magga* superiores se dividen también en 30 cada uno, las *maggavīthi* suman (30 × 4) 120. Por *bhūmi*: las 30 *sotāpattimaggavīthi* surgen en 17 *bhūmi*: las 7 *kāmasugati* y las 10 *bhūmi* *rūpāvacara* hasta *vehapphala*. Las 30 *sakadāgāmimaggavīthi* y las 30 *anāgāmimaggavīthi* surgen, además de en esas 17 *bhūmi*, también en las 4 *bhūmi* *arūpa*. Las 30 *arahattamaggavīthi* surgen, además de en esas 21 *bhūmi*, también en las 5 *bhūmi* *suddhāvāsa*. Nota: aunque se dice que en las 4 *bhūmi* *arūpa* surgen las 30 *sakadāgāmimaggavīthi*, las 30 [*anāgāmimaggavīthi*] y las 30 *arahattamaggavīthi*, en realidad en la *bhūmi* *arūpa* no surgen las 30 enteras de la *sakadāgāmimaggavīthi* y demás: como en la *bhūmi* *arūpa* hay solo el quinto *jhāna*, multiplicando la *sakadāgāmimaggapañcamajjhānavīthi* [por 2] resultan [2]; tomando eso y multiplicando por los 3, *pādakajjhāna*, *sammasitajjhāna* y *puggalajjhāsaya*, resultan 6. Así, surgen solo 6 *sakadāgāmimaggavīthi*, 6 [*anāgāmimaggavīthi*] y 6 *arahattamaggavīthi*. Por persona: las 30 *sotāpattimaggavīthi* surgen en estos 3: el *puthujjana* *tihetuka*, el *sotāpattimaggaṭṭha* y el *sotāpattiphalaṭṭha*. Las 30 [*sakadāgāmimaggavīthi*] surgen en estos 3: el *sotāpattiphalaṭṭha*, el *sakadāgāmimaggaṭṭha* y el *sakadāgāmiphalaṭṭha*. Las 30 *anāgāmimaggavīthi* surgen en estos 3: el *sakadāgāmiphalaṭṭha*, el *anāgāmimaggaṭṭha* y el *anāgāmiphalaṭṭha*. Las 30 [*arahattamaggavīthi*] surgen en estos 3: el *anāgāmiphalaṭṭha*, el *arahattamaggaṭṭha* y el *arahattaphalaṭṭha*. «*paccavekkhaṇāvīthi*». Al final de esas *maggavīthi* surgen además, según corresponda, con un *bhavaṅga* intermedio, *paccavekkhaṇāvīthi* que reflexionan sobre el *magga*, el *phala*, […] y el *nibbāna*. Esas *paccavekkhaṇāvīthi*, en resumen: después de cada uno de los 3 *magga* inferiores se obtienen 5 *vīthi* —la *vīthi* que reflexiona sobre el *magga*, la que reflexiona sobre el *phala*, la que reflexiona sobre los *kilesa* [abandonados], la que reflexiona sobre los *kilesa* restantes y la que reflexiona sobre el *nibbāna*—, y después del *arahattamagga*, 4 *vīthi* —la que reflexiona sobre el *magga*, la que reflexiona sobre el *phala*, la que reflexiona sobre [los *kilesa* abandonados] y la que reflexiona sobre el *nibbāna*—; por eso las *paccavekkhaṇāvīthi* suman 19. En detalle, en cambio: como después de cada *sotāpattimagga* hay 5 *vīthi*, después de los 30 *sotāpattimagga* hay (30 × 5) = 150. Del mismo modo, con 150 después del *sakadāgāmimagga*, 150 después del *anāgāmimagga* y 120 después del *arahattamagga*, las *paccavekkhaṇāvīthi* suman 570. Estas *paccavekkhaṇāvīthi* quedan incluidas, según corresponda, en las mismas *vīthi* *kāma* *manodvāra* antes expuestas. Por *bhūmi* y por persona, estas *paccavekkhaṇāvīthi* surgen igual que el *magga* correspondiente. «*phalasamāpattivīthi*». En ‹ဝီထိလက်ရိုး› se dice solo que la *phalasamāpattivīthi* es de 4 clases: *sotāpattiphalasamāpattivīthi*, *sakadāgāmiphalasamāpattivīthi*, *anāgāmiphalasamāpattivīthi* y *arahattaphalasamāpattivīthi*. En la *bhāsāṭīkā*, en cambio, se dice que la *phalasamāpattivīthi* es de 40 clases: tomando los 4 *phala* y multiplicando por los 5 *jhāna*, comenzando por el primer *jhāna*, resultan (4 × 5) = 20; tomando eso y multiplicando por las 2 personas, *khippābhiñña* y *dandhābhiñña*, resultan (20 × 2) 40. En el *paramatthasarūpabhedanī*, en cambio, se dice que la *phalasamāpattivīthi* es, igual que la *maggavīthi*, de 120 clases. Por *bhūmi*: las 30 [*sotāpattiphalasamāpattivīthi*] y las [30] *sakadāgāmiphalasamāpattivīthi* surgen solo en estas 21 *bhūmi*: las [7] *kāmasugati*, las 10 *rūpāvacara* hasta *vehapphala* y las 4 [*arūpa*]. Las 30 [*anāgāmiphalasamāpattivīthi*] y las 30 [*arahattaphalasamāpattivīthi*] surgen, además de en esas [21] *bhūmi*, también en las [5] *bhūmi* *suddhāvāsa*. Por persona: las 30 [*sotāpattiphalasamāpattivīthi*] surgen solo en la persona *sotāpattiphalaṭṭha* […]; las 30 [*arahattaphalasamāpattivīthi*] surgen solo en la persona *arahattaphalaṭṭha*. Así, sumadas las 120 *maggavīthi* y las 120 *phalasamāpattivīthi*, las *appanāvīthi* *lokuttara* suman (120 × 2) = 240. Sumadas las 72 *appanāvīthi* de *jhāna* y las 240 [*lokuttara*], las *appanāvīthi* suman (72 + 240) = 312. Sumadas las 10 *manodvāra* *kāmajavanavīthi* y las 312 *appanāvīthi*, las *manodvāravīthi* suman (10 + 312) = 322. Sumadas las 95 *pañcadvāravīthi* y las 322 [*manodvāravīthi*], las *vīthi* suman en total (95 + 322) 417. Nota: como las 2 clases ya expuestas [de *paccavekkhaṇāvīthi*] y la *vīthi* de *abhiññā*, […] y la *anuvattakavīthi* que se expondrán quedan ya incluidas, según corresponda, en estas [417] *vīthi* expuestas, no se cuentan aparte. «La *vīthi* de *abhiññā*». La *vīthi* de *abhiññā* y la *nirodhasamāpattivīthi* quedan también incluidas en la *jhānavīthi* (*mahaggata*). Sin embargo, solo porque su modo de surgir es particular, se exponen aparte. La *vīthi* de *abhiññā* es de 7 clases: la *vīthi* de *abhiññā* *dibbacakkhu*, *dibbasota*, *iddhividha*, *paracittavijānana*, *pubbenivāsānussati*, *yathākammupaga* y *anāgataṁsa*. De ellas, como cada una es de 4 clases —*parikammapādakajhānavīthi*, *parikammavīthi*, *abhiññāpādakajhānavīthi* y *abhiññāvīthi*—, las *vīthi* de *abhiññā* suman (7 × 4) 28. «*nirodhasamāpattivīthi*». La *nirodhasamāpattivīthi* es de 2 clases: la *nirodhasamāpattivīthi* de la persona del *kāma* y la *nirodhasamāpattivīthi* de la persona del *rūpa*. De ellas, la *nirodhasamāpattivīthi* de la persona del *kāma* es a su vez de 2 clases: la *vīthi* de la persona *anāgāmin* y la *vīthi* de la persona *arahant*. De ellas, la *vīthi* de la persona *anāgāmin* es a su vez de 2 clases: la *vīthi* de la persona aguda y la *vīthi* de la persona torpe. Del mismo modo, como la *vīthi* de la persona *arahant* es también de 2 clases, la *vīthi* de la persona aguda y la *vīthi* de la persona torpe, las *nirodhasamāpattivīthi* de la persona del *kāma* suman (2 × 2) = 4. Del mismo modo, como la *vīthi* de la persona del *rūpa* es también de 4 clases, las *nirodhasamāpattivīthi* suman (4 × 2) = 8. Por *bhūmi*, las *nirodhasamāpattivīthi* surgen solo en estas 22 *bhūmi*: las 7 *bhūmi* *kāmasugati* y las 15 *bhūmi* *rūpa*, excluida la *asaññasatta*. Por persona, surgen solo en estos 2: el *anāgāmiphalaṭṭha* y el *arahattaphalaṭṭha*. «Las *anuvattakavīthi*». Además de las *vīthi* ya expuestas, hay también *vīthi* que siguen a las *vīthi* correspondientes, llamadas *anuvattaka*. Esas *anuvattakavīthi* son de 2 clases: *pañcadvārikānuvattakavīthi* y *viññatyānuvattakavīthi*. De ellas, la *pañcadvārikānuvattakavīthi* es de 5 clases: *cakkhudvārikānuvattakavīthi*, *sotadvārikānuvattakavīthi*, *ghānadvārikānuvattakavīthi*, *jivhādvārikānuvattakavīthi* y *kāyadvārikānuvattakavīthi*. De ellas, la *cakkhudvārikānuvattakavīthi* es de 4 clases: la *atītaggahaṇamanodvāravīthi*, que toma por objeto el *rūpārammaṇa* pasado; la *samūhaggahaṇamanodvāravīthi*, que toma por objeto el conjunto de los *rūpārammaṇa*; la *atthaggahaṇamanodvāravīthi*, que toma por objeto la cosa concreta; y la *nāmaggahaṇamanodvāravīthi*, que toma por objeto el nombre, la *nāmapaññatti*. La *sotadvārikānuvattakavīthi* es a su vez (en una palabra de una sílaba, como *go*) de 3 *vīthi*: la *atītaggahaṇamanodvāravīthi*, que toma por objeto el *saddārammaṇa* pasado; la *nāmaggahaṇamanodvāravīthi*, que toma por objeto el nombre, la *nāmapaññatti* *go*; y la *atthaggahaṇamanodvāravīthi*, que toma por objeto la cosa concreta, el buey. (En una palabra de dos sílabas, como *ghaṭa*) es de 5 *vīthi*: la *atītaggahaṇamanodvāravīthi*, que toma por objeto el *saddārammaṇa* pasado *gha*; la *atītaggahaṇamanodvāravīthi*, que toma por objeto el *saddārammaṇa* pasado *ṭa*; la *samūhaggahaṇamanodvāravīthi*, que toma por objeto el conjunto de los *saddārammaṇa* pasados *ghaṭa*; la *nāmaggahaṇamanodvāravīthi*, que toma por objeto el nombre, la *nāmapaññatti* *ghaṭa*; y la *atthaggahaṇamanodvāravīthi*, que toma por objeto la cosa concreta, la vasija. (En una palabra de tres sílabas, como *purisa*) es de 6 *vīthi*: la *atītaggahaṇamanodvāravīthi*, que toma por objeto el *saddārammaṇa* pasado *pu*; la que toma por objeto el *saddārammaṇa* pasado *ri*; la que toma por objeto el *saddārammaṇa* pasado *sa*; la *samūhaggahaṇamanodvāravīthi*, que toma por objeto el conjunto de los *saddārammaṇa* pasados *purisa*; la [*nāmaggahaṇamanodvāravīthi*], que toma por objeto el nombre, la *nāmapaññatti* *purisa*; y la *atthaggahaṇamanodvāravīthi*, que toma por objeto la cosa concreta, el hombre. Y así sucesivamente: por cada sílaba que se añade, se añade una *atītaggahaṇamanodvāravīthi*. La *ghānadvārikānuvattakavīthi*, la *jivhādvārikānuvattakavīthi* y la *kāyadvārikānuvattakavīthi* son también, cada una, como la *cakkhudvārikānuvattakavīthi*, de 4 clases: *atītaggahaṇamanodvāravīthi*, *samūhaggahaṇamanodvāravīthi*, *atthaggahaṇamanodvāravīthi* y *nāmaggahaṇamanodvāravīthi*. La *viññatyānuvattakavīthi* es a su vez de 2 clases: *kāyaviññatyānuvattakavīthi* y *vacīviññatyānuvattakavīthi*. De ellas, la *kāyaviññatyānuvattakavīthi* es de 5 clases: la *atītaggahaṇamanodvāravīthi*, que toma por objeto el *rūpārammaṇa* pasado; la *samūhaggahaṇamanodvāravīthi*, que toma por objeto el conjunto de los *rūpārammaṇa*; la *atthaggahaṇamanodvāravīthi*, que toma por objeto la cosa concreta; la *viññattiggahaṇamanodvāravīthi*, que toma por objeto la *kāyaviññatti*; y la *adhippāyaggahaṇamanodvāravīthi*, que toma por objeto el deseo / la intención de la persona que hace la *viññatti*. La *vacīviññatyānuvattakavīthi* es a su vez (en una palabra de una sílaba) de 5 clases: la *atītaggahaṇamanodvāravīthi*, que toma por objeto el *saddārammaṇa* pasado; la *nāmaggahaṇamanodvāravīthi*, que toma por objeto el nombre, la *nāmapaññatti*; la *atthaggahaṇamanodvāravīthi*, que toma por objeto la cosa concreta; la *viññattiggahaṇamanodvāravīthi*, que toma por objeto la *vacīviññatti*; y la *adhippāyaggahaṇamanodvāravīthi*, que toma por objeto el deseo / la intención de la persona que hace la *viññatti*. (En una palabra de dos sílabas) es de 7 clases: 2 *vīthi* *atītaggahaṇamanodvāra*, que toman por objeto el *saddārammaṇa* pasado de cada sílaba; la *samūhaggahaṇamanodvāravīthi*, que toma por objeto el conjunto de los *saddārammaṇa* pasados que son las 2 sílabas; la *nāmaggahaṇamanodvāravīthi*, que toma por objeto el nombre, la *nāmapaññatti*; la *atthaggahaṇamanodvāravīthi*, que toma por objeto la cosa concreta; la *viññattiggahaṇamanodvāravīthi*, que toma por objeto la *vacīviññatti*; y la *adhippāyaggahaṇamanodvāravīthi*, que toma por objeto el deseo / la intención de la persona que hace la *viññatti*. Y así sucesivamente: por cada sílaba que se añade, se añade una *vīthi* *atītaggahaṇamanodvāra*. Estas *anuvattakavīthi* quedan incluidas, según corresponda, en las mismas *vīthi* *kāma* *manodvāra* antes expuestas.
en: (1) road, route; road / route / way; roads in general; side road, street within a town or village; lane; footpath; ordinary road. (2) main road; main road, broad / great road. (3) (along which the moon, the sun, the constellations, the stars and so on travel) path. The path of the planets; the path of the sky. (The paths along which the moon and the sun travel are of three kinds: (1) *ajavīthi* = the path of the moon and sun resembling a goat, or the path of the moon and sun in the season suited to the goat; (2) *nāgavīthi* = the path of the moon and sun resembling an elephant, or the path of the moon and sun in the season suited to the elephant; (3) *govīthi* = the path of the moon and sun resembling an ox, or the path of the moon and sun in the season suited to the ox. Headwords *ajavīthi*, *nāgavīthi*, *govīthi*.) (4) the path that is the *ariyamagga*. (5) (a) the path / established road / right road that is the *kammaṭṭhāna*. (b) the path / established road / right road that is *bhāvanā*. (c) the path / established road / right road that is *vipassanā*. See also [[vipassanāvīthi]]. (6) the path that is the *saccā* / of the *saccā* (the true object called *diṭṭha*, *suta*, *muta*, *viññāta*, *adiṭṭha*, *asuta*, *amuta*, *aviññāta*). (7) (a) succession. (b) the succession / series of minds; the *vīthi* (beginning with the *cakkhudvāravīthi*). (See [[vīthicitta]] and the other headwords.) The succession of minds beginning with *atītabhavaṅga*, *bhavaṅgacalana*, *bhavaṅgupaccheda*, *pañcadvārāvajjana*, *cakkhuviññāṇa*, *sampaṭicchana*, *javana* seven times and *tadārammaṇa* twice is, in accordance with the verbal definition '…', called *vīthi* because it resembles a route: just as the road along which beings travel goes on without skipping the succession of villages, one mind does not skip over another but occurs only in its order. That *vīthi* is of 2 kinds: *pañcadvāravīthi* and *manodvāravīthi*. Of these, the *pañcadvāravīthi* is of 5 kinds: *cakkhudvāravīthi*, *sotadvāravīthi*, *ghānadvāravīthi*, *jivhādvāravīthi* and *kāyadvāravīthi*. Of these, the *cakkhudvāravīthi* is of 2 kinds: the *vīthi* in which no *āgantukabhavaṅga* occurs and the *vīthi* in which *āgantukabhavaṅga* occurs. Of these, the *vīthi* in which no *āgantukabhavaṅga* occurs is of 4 kinds: *atimahantārammaṇavīthi*, *mahantārammaṇavīthi*, *parittārammaṇavīthi* and *atiparittārammaṇavīthi*. Of these, the *atimahantārammaṇavīthi* is of 2 kinds: *tadārammaṇavāra* and *javanavāra*. The *mahantārammaṇavīthi* is of 2 kinds: the *vīthi* in which *atītabhavaṅga* has passed 2 times and the *vīthi* in which it has passed 3 times. The *parittārammaṇavīthi* is of 6 kinds: from the *vīthi* in which *atītabhavaṅga* has passed 4 times to the *vīthi* in which it has passed 9 times. The *atiparittārammaṇavīthi*: from the *vīthi* in which *atītabhavaṅga* has passed 10 times to the *vīthi* in which it has passed 15 times […]. The *cakkhudvāravīthi* in which no *āgantukabhavaṅga* occurs total 16. The *vīthi* in which *āgantukabhavaṅga* occurs is of 2 kinds: *atimahantārammaṇavīthi* and *mahantārammaṇavīthi*. Of these, the *atimahantārammaṇavīthi* is of one kind only: the *vīthi* in which *atītabhavaṅga* has passed 1 time. The *mahantārammaṇavīthi* is of 2 kinds: the *vīthi* in which *atītabhavaṅga* has passed 2 times and the *vīthi* in which it has passed 3 times. Thus the *cakkhudvāravīthi* in which *āgantukabhavaṅga* occurs total 3. Adding the 2, the *vīthi* in which no *āgantukabhavaṅga* occurs and the *vīthi* in which it occurs, the *cakkhudvāravīthi* total (16 + 3) 19. Likewise, since the *sotadvāravīthi*, *ghānadvāravīthi*, *jivhādvāravīthi* and *kāyadvāravīthi* are also of 19 kinds each, the *pañcadvāravīthi* total (19 × 5) 95. By *bhūmi*: of those 5 kinds of *vīthi*, these 65 *vīthi* —the *cakkhudvāra* *atimahantārammaṇavīthi* *tadārammaṇavāra* (1), the [*cakkhudvāravīthi*] in which *āgantukabhavaṅga* occurs (3), the *sotadvāra* *atimahantārammaṇavīthi* *tadārammaṇavāra* (1), the *sotadvāravīthi* in which *āgantukabhavaṅga* occurs (3), the *ghānadvāravīthi* (19), the *jivhādvāravīthi* (19) and the *kāyadvāravīthi* (19)— occur only in the 11 *kāma* *bhūmi*. The remaining 30 occur in the 26 *pañcavokāra* *bhūmi*. By person: the 95 occur in the 4 *puthujjana* and the 4 *phalaṭṭha*, 8 persons in all. The *manodvāravīthi* in turn is of 2 kinds: *kāmajavanavīthi* and *appanājavanavīthi*. Of these, the *kāmajavanavīthi* is of 9 kinds: in the object that is the 22 present *rūpa* able to last seventeen [moments], excluding the two *viññatti* and the [4] *lakkhaṇarūpa*, the *vibhūtārammaṇa* (5) and [*avibhūtārammaṇa*] (2) *vīthi*; in the object that is the remaining *rūpa*, unable to last seventeen [moments], *nāma* and *paññatti*, the *vibhūtārammaṇa* (1) and [*avibhūtārammaṇa*] (1) *vīthi*. By *bhūmi*: the 6 *vibhūtārammaṇa* *vīthi* occur only in the [11] *kāma* *bhūmi*; the 3 *avibhūtārammaṇa* *vīthi* occur in the 30 *bhūmi* excluding the *asaññasatta*. By person: the 9 *manodvāravīthi* occur in these 8: the 4 *puthujjana* and the 4 *phalaṭṭha*. The dream *vīthi* (or …): in accordance with '…' and '…', when in a dream it is as if one sees, as if one hears, taking as object some one unnoticed object among the 6 objects, *bhavaṅgacalana*, *bhavaṅgupaccheda* and *manodvārāvajjana* occur, [and the *javana*] 2 or 3 times, after which *bhavaṅga* occurs as much as is due: there is also this one more kind, the *abyākata* *manodvāra* *avibhūtārammaṇa* *vīthi*. Counting that *vīthi* too, the *manodvāra* *kāmajavana* *vīthi* total 10. By *bhūmi*, the dream *vīthi* occurs only in the human *bhūmi*; by person, the dream *vīthi* occurs only in these 7: the 4 *puthujjana*, the *sotāpattiphalaṭṭha*, the *sakadāgāmiphalaṭṭha* and the *anāgāmiphalaṭṭha*. The *maraṇāsannavīthi* is also included, as appropriate, in these same *kāmāvacara* *vīthi*. Therefore that *maraṇāsannavīthi* is of 2 kinds: *pañcadvāravīthi* and *manodvāravīthi*. Of these, the *pañcadvāravīthi* is of 5 kinds: *cakkhudvāravīthi*, *sotadvāravīthi*, *ghānadvāravīthi*, *jivhādvāravīthi* and *kāyadvāravīthi*. Of these, the *cakkhudvāravīthi* is of 4 kinds: the *vīthi* in which *cuti* occurs after *javana*; the *vīthi* in which *cuti* occurs after *javana* and *bhavaṅga*; the *vīthi* in which *cuti* occurs after *tadārammaṇa*; and the *vīthi* in which *cuti* occurs after *tadārammaṇa* and *bhavaṅga*. Likewise, since the *sotadvāravīthi*, *ghānadvāravīthi*, *jivhādvāravīthi* and *kāyadvāravīthi* are also of 4 kinds each, the *pañcadvāra* *maraṇāsannavīthi* total (5 × 4) 20. (Note: ‹ဝီထိလက်ရိုး› and the *paramatthasarūpabhedanī* say that these 20 *pañcadvāra* *maraṇāsannavīthi* occur only in the 4 *puthujjana* and the 2 lower *phalaṭṭha* who, dying in the *kāma* *bhūmi*, are to arise in the *kāma* *bhūmi*. The *bhāsāṭīkā*, however, says that of those 20 *vīthi* these 4 —the *cakkhudvāravīthi* and *sotadvāravīthi* in which *cuti* occurs after *javana*, and the *cakkhudvāravīthi* and *sotadvāravīthi* in which *cuti* occurs after *javana* and *bhavaṅga*— occur [in those who], dying in the 10 *bhūmi* up to *vehapphala*, [arise] in the *kāmasugati* *bhūmi*.) The *manodvāravīthi* in turn is of 2 kinds: the *maraṇāsannavīthi* of *puthujjana* and *sekkha*, and the *maraṇāsannavīthi* of *arahant*. Of these, the *maraṇāsannavīthi* of *puthujjana* and *sekkha* is of 9 kinds: (1) the *vīthi* of these 6: the 4 *puthujjana* and the 2 lower *phalaṭṭha* who, dying in the 11 *kāma* *bhūmi*, are to arise in the 11 *kāma* *bhūmi*; (2) the *vīthi* of these 4: the *tihetuka* *puthujjana* and the 3 lower *phalaṭṭha* who, dying in the 7 *kāmasugati* *bhūmi*, are to arise in the 15 *rūpa* *bhūmi* excluding the *asaññasatta*; (3) the *vīthi* of the *tihetuka* *puthujjana* who, dying in the 7 *kāmasugati* *bhūmi*, is to arise in the *asaññasatta* *bhūmi*; (4) the *vīthi* of these 4: the *tihetuka* *puthujjana* and the 3 lower *phalaṭṭha* who, dying in the 7 *kāmasugati* *bhūmi*, are to arise in the 4 *arūpa* *bhūmi*; (5) the *vīthi* of these 4: the *tihetuka* *puthujjana* and the 3 lower *phalaṭṭha* who, dying in the 15 *rūpa* *bhūmi* excluding the *asaññasatta*, are to arise in the 15 *rūpa* *bhūmi* excluding the *asaññasatta*; (6) the *vīthi* of the *tihetuka* *puthujjana* who, dying in the 10 *rūpa* *bhūmi* up to *vehapphala*, is to arise in the 7 *kāmasugati* *bhūmi*; (7) the *vīthi* of these 4: the *tihetuka* *puthujjana* and the 3 lower *phalaṭṭha* who, dying in the 10 *rūpa* *bhūmi* up to *vehapphala*, are to arise in the 4 *arūpa* *bhūmi*; (8) the *vīthi* of these 4: the *tihetuka* *puthujjana* and the 3 lower *phalaṭṭha* who, dying in the 4 *arūpa* *bhūmi*, are to arise in the 4 *arūpa* *bhūmi*; (9) the *vīthi* of the *tihetuka* *puthujjana* who, dying in the 4 *arūpa* *bhūmi*, is to arise in the 7 *kāmasugati* *bhūmi*. Of these, the *vīthi* of the 6 —the 4 *puthujjana* and the 2 lower *phalaṭṭha* who, dying in the 11 *kāma* *bhūmi*, are to arise in the 11 *bhūmi*— is of 4 kinds: the *vīthi* (1) after *javana*, (2) after *javana* and *bhavaṅga*, (3) after *tadārammaṇa*, (4) after *tadārammaṇa* and *bhavaṅga*. Of the remaining 8 *vīthi*, each divides into 2: (1) the *vīthi* in which *cuti* occurs after *javana*, (2) the *vīthi* in which *cuti* occurs after *javana* and *bhavaṅga*; therefore the *manodvāra* *maraṇāsannavīthi* of *puthujjana* and *sekkha* total (4 + 16) = 20. The *maraṇāsannavīthi* of *arahant* in turn is of 3 kinds: (1) the *vīthi* of *arahant* dwelling in the *kāma* *bhūmi*, (2) the *vīthi* of *arahant* dwelling in the *rūpa* *bhūmi*, (3) the *vīthi* of *arahant* dwelling in the *arūpa* *bhūmi*. Of these, the *vīthi* of *arahant* dwelling in the *kāma* *bhūmi* is of 4 kinds: the *vīthi* in which *cuti* occurs (1) after *javana*, (2) after *javana* and *bhavaṅga*, (3) after *tadārammaṇa*, (4) after *tadārammaṇa* and *bhavaṅga*. Of the remaining 2 *vīthi*, each divides into 2: (1) the *vīthi* in which *cuti* occurs after *javana*, (2) the *vīthi* in which *cuti* occurs after *javana* and *bhavaṅga*; therefore the *manodvāra* *maraṇāsannavīthi* of *arahant* total (4 + 4) 8. Thus, adding the 2, the *maraṇāsannavīthi* of *puthujjana* and *sekkha* and that of *arahant*, the *manodvāra* *maraṇāsannavīthi* total (20 + 8) = 28. Adding the 2, the *pañcadvāra* *maraṇāsannavīthi* and the *manodvāra* *maraṇāsannavīthi*, the *maraṇāsannavīthi* total (20 + 28) = 48. Note: the *vīthi* of the *ahetuka* *puthujjana* of happy destiny who, dying in the *asaññasatta* *bhūmi*, is to arise in the 7 *kāmasugati* *bhūmi* has been left out, because there is *nāma* only in the new existence and no *nāma* in the old existence. Note that, counting it too, the *maraṇāsannavīthi* total 49. '*appanāvīthi*'. The *appanāvīthi* in turn is of 5 kinds: *jhānavīthi*, *maggavīthi*, *phalasamāpattivīthi*, *abhiññāvīthi* and *nirodhasamāpattivīthi*. Of these, the *jhānavīthi* is of 2 kinds: *ādikammikavīthi* and *samāpattivīthi*. Of these, the *ādikammikavīthi* is of 9 kinds: (1) *rūpapaṭhamajjhānavīthi*, (2) *rūpadutiyajjhānavīthi*, (3) *rūpatatiyajjhānavīthi*, (4) *rūpacatutthajjhānavīthi*, (5) […], (6) […], (7) *viññāṇañcāyatanajjhānavīthi*, (8) *ākiñcaññāyatanajjhānavīthi*, (9) *nevasaññānāsaññāyatanajjhānavīthi*. Of these, each divides into 2, as wholesome and *kiriya*; therefore, taking those 9 *jhāna* and multiplying by 2, the *ādikammika* *jhāna* *vīthi* total (9 × 2) 18. Of those 18, each divides into 2, the *vīthi* of the keen person and the *vīthi* of the dull person; therefore, taking those 18 and multiplying by 2, the *ādikammika* *jhāna* *vīthi* total (18 × 2) 36. Likewise, since the *samāpattivīthi* is also of 36 kinds, adding the 2, the *jhānavīthi* total (36 × 2) 72. (Included here are 8 *vīthi* of the first *jhāna*, 8 *vīthi* of the second *jhāna*, 8 of the third *jhāna*, 8 *vīthi* of the [fourth] *jhāna* and 40 *vīthi* of the fifth *jhāna*.) By *bhūmi*: of those 72 *jhānavīthi*, the 4 *paṭhamajjhānaādikammikavīthi* occur only in the 7 *kāmasugati* *bhūmi*. The 4 *dutiyajjhānaādikammikavīthi* and the 4 *tatiyajjhānaādikammikavīthi* occur only in the 7 *kāmasugati* *bhūmi* and the 3 first-*jhāna* *bhūmi*. The 4 *catutthajjhānaādikammikavīthi* occur only in the 7 *kāmasugati* *bhūmi*, the 3 first-*jhāna* *bhūmi* and the 3 second-*jhāna* *bhūmi*. The *pañcamajjhānaādikammikavīthi* occurs only in the 7 *kāmasugati* *bhūmi*, the 3 first-*jhāna* *bhūmi*, the 3 second-*jhāna* *bhūmi* and the 3 third-*jhāna* *bhūmi*. The 4 *ākāsānañcāyatanaādikammikavīthi* occur only in the 7 *kāmasugati* *bhūmi* and the [15] *rūpa* *bhūmi* excluding the *asaññasatta*. […] the 4 occur only in the 7 *kāmasugati* *bhūmi*, the 15 *rūpa* *bhūmi* excluding the *asaññasatta*, and the *ākāsānañcāyatana* *bhūmi*. […] the 4 occur only in the [7] *kāmasugati* *bhūmi*, the [15] *rūpa* *bhūmi* excluding the *asaññasatta*, the *ākāsānañcāyatana* *bhūmi* and the *viññāṇañcāyatana* *bhūmi*. […] the 4 occur only in the 7 *kāmasugati* *bhūmi*, the [15] *bhūmi* excluding the *asaññasatta*, the *ākāsānañcāyatana* *bhūmi*, the *viññāṇañcāyatana* *bhūmi* and the *ākiñcaññāyatana* *bhūmi*. As for the *samāpattivīthi*, in the [7] *kāmasugati* *bhūmi* and the [15] *rūpa* *bhūmi* excluding the *asaññasatta*, all 36 *samāpattivīthi* occur. In the *ākāsānañcāyatana* *bhūmi* only 16 occur. In the *viññāṇañcāyatana* *bhūmi* only 4, 4 and 4, 12 *samāpattivīthi* in all, occur. In the *ākiñcaññāyatana* *bhūmi* only 4 and 4, 8 *samāpattivīthi* in all, occur. In the *nevasaññānāsaññāyatana* *bhūmi* only 4 occur. By person: the 72 *jhānavīthi* occur in these 5 persons: the *tihetuka* *puthujjana* person and the 4 *phalaṭṭha* persons. '*paccavekkhaṇāvīthi*'. At the end of those *jhānavīthi* there also occur, as appropriate, with *bhavaṅga* intervening, *paccavekkhaṇāvīthi* that reflect on the factors of the *jhāna*. Since those *paccavekkhaṇāvīthi* are obtained one *vīthi* for each factor of the *jhāna*, after the 8 *vīthi* of the first *jhāna* there are (8 × 5) = 40; after the 8 *vīthi* of the second *jhāna*, (8 × 4) = 32; after the 8 *vīthi* of the third *jhāna*, (8 × 3) 24; after the 8 *vīthi* of the fourth *jhāna*, (8 × 2) = 16; after the 40 *vīthi* of the fifth *jhāna*, (40 × 2) = 80: the *paccavekkhaṇāvīthi* total 192. By *bhūmi* and by person, the *paccavekkhaṇāvīthi* occur like the corresponding *jhānavīthi*. These *paccavekkhaṇāvīthi* are included, as appropriate, in the same *kāma* *manodvāra* *vīthi* stated earlier. Note: ‹ဝီထိလက်ရိုး› and ‹ဝီထိပုံ› speak of the *paccavekkhaṇāvīthi* only immediately after the *ādikammika* *jhāna* *vīthi*; the *paramatthasarūpabhedanī* and the *bhāsāṭīkā*, however, speak of the *paccavekkhaṇāvīthi* also immediately after the *samāpattivīthi*. '*maggavīthi*'. The *maggavīthi* is of 4 kinds: *sotāpattimaggavīthi*, *sakadāgāmimaggavīthi*, *anāgāmimaggavīthi* and *arahattamaggavīthi*. Of these, the *sotāpattimaggavīthi* is of 5 kinds: *paṭhamajjhānavīthi*, *dutiyajjhānavīthi*, *tatiyajjhānavīthi*, *catutthajjhānavīthi* and *pañcamajjhānavīthi*. Of these, each divides into 2, the *vīthi* of the keen person and the *vīthi* of the dull person; therefore, taking the 5 that are divided by way of the *jhāna* and multiplying by 2, there are 10. Of those 10 *sotāpattimaggavīthi*, each divides into 3 by way of the *pādakajjhāna*, the *sammasitajjhāna* and the *puggalajjhāsaya*; therefore, taking the 10 and multiplying by 3, the *sotāpattimaggavīthi* total 30. Likewise, since the 3 higher *magga* also divide into 30 each, the *maggavīthi* total (30 × 4) 120. By *bhūmi*: the 30 *sotāpattimaggavīthi* occur in 17 *bhūmi*: the 7 *kāmasugati* and the 10 *rūpāvacara* *bhūmi* up to *vehapphala*. The 30 *sakadāgāmimaggavīthi* and the 30 *anāgāmimaggavīthi* occur, besides those 17 *bhūmi*, also in the 4 *arūpa* *bhūmi*. The 30 *arahattamaggavīthi* occur, besides those 21 *bhūmi*, also in the 5 *suddhāvāsa* *bhūmi*. Note: although it is said that in the 4 *arūpa* *bhūmi* the 30 *sakadāgāmimaggavīthi*, the 30 [*anāgāmimaggavīthi*] and the 30 *arahattamaggavīthi* occur, in truth not all 30 of the *sakadāgāmimaggavīthi* and so on occur in the *arūpa* *bhūmi*: since in the *arūpa* *bhūmi* there is only the fifth *jhāna*, multiplying the *sakadāgāmimaggapañcamajjhānavīthi* [by 2] gives [2]; taking that and multiplying by the 3, *pādakajjhāna*, *sammasitajjhāna* and *puggalajjhāsaya*, gives 6. Thus only 6 *sakadāgāmimaggavīthi*, 6 [*anāgāmimaggavīthi*] and 6 *arahattamaggavīthi* occur. By person: the 30 *sotāpattimaggavīthi* occur in these 3: the *tihetuka* *puthujjana*, the *sotāpattimaggaṭṭha* and the *sotāpattiphalaṭṭha*. The 30 [*sakadāgāmimaggavīthi*] occur in these 3: the *sotāpattiphalaṭṭha*, the *sakadāgāmimaggaṭṭha* and the *sakadāgāmiphalaṭṭha*. The 30 *anāgāmimaggavīthi* occur in these 3: the *sakadāgāmiphalaṭṭha*, the *anāgāmimaggaṭṭha* and the *anāgāmiphalaṭṭha*. The 30 [*arahattamaggavīthi*] occur in these 3: the *anāgāmiphalaṭṭha*, the *arahattamaggaṭṭha* and the *arahattaphalaṭṭha*. '*paccavekkhaṇāvīthi*'. At the end of those *maggavīthi* there also occur, as appropriate, with *bhavaṅga* intervening, *paccavekkhaṇāvīthi* that reflect on the *magga*, the *phala*, […] and *nibbāna*. Those *paccavekkhaṇāvīthi*, in brief: after each of the 3 lower *magga*, 5 *vīthi* are obtained —the *vīthi* reflecting on the *magga*, the one reflecting on the *phala*, the one reflecting on the [abandoned] *kilesa*, the one reflecting on the remaining *kilesa* and the one reflecting on *nibbāna*—, and after the *arahattamagga* 4 *vīthi* —the one reflecting on the *magga*, the one reflecting on the *phala*, the one reflecting on [the abandoned *kilesa*] and the one reflecting on *nibbāna*—; therefore the *paccavekkhaṇāvīthi* total 19. In detail, however: since after each *sotāpattimagga* there are 5 *vīthi*, after the 30 *sotāpattimagga* there are (30 × 5) = 150. Likewise, with 150 after the *sakadāgāmimagga*, 150 after the *anāgāmimagga* and 120 after the *arahattamagga*, the *paccavekkhaṇāvīthi* total 570. These *paccavekkhaṇāvīthi* are included, as appropriate, in the same *kāma* *manodvāra* *vīthi* stated earlier. By *bhūmi* and by person, these *paccavekkhaṇāvīthi* occur like the corresponding *magga*. '*phalasamāpattivīthi*'. ‹ဝီထိလက်ရိုး› says only that the *phalasamāpattivīthi* is of 4 kinds: *sotāpattiphalasamāpattivīthi*, *sakadāgāmiphalasamāpattivīthi*, *anāgāmiphalasamāpattivīthi* and *arahattaphalasamāpattivīthi*. The *bhāsāṭīkā*, however, says that the *phalasamāpattivīthi* is of 40 kinds: taking the 4 *phala* and multiplying by the 5 *jhāna* beginning with the first *jhāna* gives (4 × 5) = 20; taking that and multiplying by the 2 persons, *khippābhiñña* and *dandhābhiñña*, gives (20 × 2) 40. The *paramatthasarūpabhedanī*, however, says that the *phalasamāpattivīthi*, like the *maggavīthi*, is of 120 kinds. By *bhūmi*: the 30 [*sotāpattiphalasamāpattivīthi*] and the [30] *sakadāgāmiphalasamāpattivīthi* occur only in these 21 *bhūmi*: the [7] *kāmasugati*, the 10 *rūpāvacara* up to *vehapphala* and the 4 [*arūpa*]. The 30 [*anāgāmiphalasamāpattivīthi*] and the 30 [*arahattaphalasamāpattivīthi*] occur, besides those [21] *bhūmi*, also in the [5] *suddhāvāsa* *bhūmi*. By person: the 30 [*sotāpattiphalasamāpattivīthi*] occur only in the *sotāpattiphalaṭṭha* person […]; the 30 [*arahattaphalasamāpattivīthi*] occur only in the *arahattaphalaṭṭha* person. Thus, adding the 120 *maggavīthi* and the 120 *phalasamāpattivīthi*, the *lokuttara* *appanāvīthi* total (120 × 2) = 240. Adding the 72 *jhāna* *appanāvīthi* and the 240 [*lokuttara*], the *appanāvīthi* total (72 + 240) = 312. Adding the 10 *manodvāra* *kāmajavanavīthi* and the 312 *appanāvīthi*, the *manodvāravīthi* total (10 + 312) = 322. Adding the 95 *pañcadvāravīthi* and the 322 [*manodvāravīthi*], the *vīthi* total in all (95 + 322) 417. Note: since the 2 kinds already stated [of *paccavekkhaṇāvīthi*] and the *abhiññā* *vīthi*, […] and the *anuvattakavīthi* to be stated are already included, as appropriate, in these [417] *vīthi* stated, they are not counted separately. 'The *abhiññā* *vīthi*'. The *abhiññā* *vīthi* and the *nirodhasamāpattivīthi* are also included within the (*mahaggata*) *jhānavīthi*. However, only because their manner of occurring is special are they set out separately. The *abhiññā* *vīthi* is of 7 kinds: the *dibbacakkhu*, *dibbasota*, *iddhividha*, *paracittavijānana*, *pubbenivāsānussati*, *yathākammupaga* and *anāgataṁsa* *abhiññā* *vīthi*. Of these, since each is of 4 kinds —*parikammapādakajhānavīthi*, *parikammavīthi*, *abhiññāpādakajhānavīthi* and *abhiññāvīthi*—, the *abhiññā* *vīthi* total (7 × 4) 28. '*nirodhasamāpattivīthi*'. The *nirodhasamāpattivīthi* is of 2 kinds: the *nirodhasamāpattivīthi* of the *kāma* person and the *nirodhasamāpattivīthi* of the *rūpa* person. Of these, the *nirodhasamāpattivīthi* of the *kāma* person is in turn of 2 kinds: the *vīthi* of the *anāgāmin* person and the *vīthi* of the *arahant* person. Of these, the *vīthi* of the *anāgāmin* person is in turn of 2 kinds: the *vīthi* of the keen person and the *vīthi* of the dull person. Likewise, since the *vīthi* of the *arahant* person is also of 2 kinds, the *vīthi* of the keen person and the *vīthi* of the dull person, the *nirodhasamāpattivīthi* of the *kāma* person total (2 × 2) = 4. Likewise, since the *vīthi* of the *rūpa* person is also of 4 kinds, the *nirodhasamāpattivīthi* total (4 × 2) = 8. By *bhūmi*, the *nirodhasamāpattivīthi* occur only in these 22 *bhūmi*: the 7 *kāmasugati* *bhūmi* and the 15 *rūpa* *bhūmi* excluding the *asaññasatta*. By person, they occur only in these 2: the *anāgāmiphalaṭṭha* and the *arahattaphalaṭṭha*. 'The *anuvattakavīthi*'. Besides the *vīthi* already stated, there are also *vīthi* that follow the corresponding *vīthi*, called *anuvattaka*. Those *anuvattakavīthi* are of 2 kinds: *pañcadvārikānuvattakavīthi* and *viññatyānuvattakavīthi*. Of these, the *pañcadvārikānuvattakavīthi* is of 5 kinds: *cakkhudvārikānuvattakavīthi*, *sotadvārikānuvattakavīthi*, *ghānadvārikānuvattakavīthi*, *jivhādvārikānuvattakavīthi* and *kāyadvārikānuvattakavīthi*. Of these, the *cakkhudvārikānuvattakavīthi* is of 4 kinds: the *atītaggahaṇamanodvāravīthi*, taking as object the past *rūpārammaṇa*; the *samūhaggahaṇamanodvāravīthi*, taking as object the aggregate of *rūpārammaṇa*; the *atthaggahaṇamanodvāravīthi*, taking as object the concrete thing; and the *nāmaggahaṇamanodvāravīthi*, taking as object the name, the *nāmapaññatti*. The *sotadvārikānuvattakavīthi* in turn (in a word of one syllable, such as *go*) consists of 3 *vīthi*: the *atītaggahaṇamanodvāravīthi*, taking as object the past *saddārammaṇa*; the *nāmaggahaṇamanodvāravīthi*, taking as object the name, the *nāmapaññatti* *go*; and the *atthaggahaṇamanodvāravīthi*, taking as object the concrete thing, the ox. (In a word of two syllables, such as *ghaṭa*) it consists of 5 *vīthi*: the *atītaggahaṇamanodvāravīthi*, taking as object the past *saddārammaṇa* *gha*; the *atītaggahaṇamanodvāravīthi*, taking as object the past *saddārammaṇa* *ṭa*; the *samūhaggahaṇamanodvāravīthi*, taking as object the aggregate of past *saddārammaṇa* *ghaṭa*; the *nāmaggahaṇamanodvāravīthi*, taking as object the name, the *nāmapaññatti* *ghaṭa*; and the *atthaggahaṇamanodvāravīthi*, taking as object the concrete thing, the pot. (In a word of three syllables, such as *purisa*) it consists of 6 *vīthi*: the *atītaggahaṇamanodvāravīthi*, taking as object the past *saddārammaṇa* *pu*; the one taking as object the past *saddārammaṇa* *ri*; the one taking as object the past *saddārammaṇa* *sa*; the *samūhaggahaṇamanodvāravīthi*, taking as object the aggregate of past *saddārammaṇa* *purisa*; the [*nāmaggahaṇamanodvāravīthi*], taking as object the name, the *nāmapaññatti* *purisa*; and the *atthaggahaṇamanodvāravīthi*, taking as object the concrete thing, the man. And so on: for every syllable added, one *atītaggahaṇamanodvāravīthi* is added. The *ghānadvārikānuvattakavīthi*, the *jivhādvārikānuvattakavīthi* and the *kāyadvārikānuvattakavīthi* are also each, like the *cakkhudvārikānuvattakavīthi*, of 4 kinds: *atītaggahaṇamanodvāravīthi*, *samūhaggahaṇamanodvāravīthi*, *atthaggahaṇamanodvāravīthi* and *nāmaggahaṇamanodvāravīthi*. The *viññatyānuvattakavīthi* in turn is of 2 kinds: *kāyaviññatyānuvattakavīthi* and *vacīviññatyānuvattakavīthi*. Of these, the *kāyaviññatyānuvattakavīthi* is of 5 kinds: the *atītaggahaṇamanodvāravīthi*, taking as object the past *rūpārammaṇa*; the *samūhaggahaṇamanodvāravīthi*, taking as object the aggregate of *rūpārammaṇa*; the *atthaggahaṇamanodvāravīthi*, taking as object the concrete thing; the *viññattiggahaṇamanodvāravīthi*, taking as object the *kāyaviññatti*; and the *adhippāyaggahaṇamanodvāravīthi*, taking as object the wish / intention of the person making the *viññatti*. The *vacīviññatyānuvattakavīthi* in turn (in a word of one syllable) is of 5 kinds: the *atītaggahaṇamanodvāravīthi*, taking as object the past *saddārammaṇa*; the *nāmaggahaṇamanodvāravīthi*, taking as object the name, the *nāmapaññatti*; the *atthaggahaṇamanodvāravīthi*, taking as object the concrete thing; the *viññattiggahaṇamanodvāravīthi*, taking as object the *vacīviññatti*; and the *adhippāyaggahaṇamanodvāravīthi*, taking as object the wish / intention of the person making the *viññatti*. (In a word of two syllables) it is of 7 kinds: 2 *atītaggahaṇamanodvāra* *vīthi*, taking as object the past *saddārammaṇa* of each syllable; the *samūhaggahaṇamanodvāravīthi*, taking as object the aggregate of past *saddārammaṇa* that is the 2 syllables; the *nāmaggahaṇamanodvāravīthi*, taking as object the name, the *nāmapaññatti*; the *atthaggahaṇamanodvāravīthi*, taking as object the concrete thing; the *viññattiggahaṇamanodvāravīthi*, taking as object the *vacīviññatti*; and the *adhippāyaggahaṇamanodvāravīthi*, taking as object the wish / intention of the person making the *viññatti*. And so on: for every syllable added, one *atītaggahaṇamanodvāra* *vīthi* is added. These *anuvattakavīthi* are included, as appropriate, in the same *kāma* *manodvāra* *vīthi* stated earlier.

(d) *paññā* apt to explore / reflect on / scrutinize / know the cause / matter that has arisen. (e) *paññā* apt to explore / reflect on / scrutinize / know the four *saccā*. (f) *paññā* apt to explore / reflect on / scrutinize / know the nature of each of the *paramattha* states. (g) *paññā* apt to explore / reflect on / scrutinize / know the groups of states. (6) *vīmaṁsādhipati*. (7) *vīmaṁsiddhipāda*. See [[vīmaṁsiddhipāda]]. (8) the tip of an elephant's trunk.
