es: el desmayarse / el quedar aturdido; el emitir los sonidos en grave y agudo / el cantar y tocar. Véase también [[mucchana]]. (Los sonidos que se cantan y tocan son: (1) el sonido *usabha*, sonido como el mugido de los bueyes; (2) el sonido *dhevata*, sonido como el relincho de los caballos; (3) el sonido *chajja*, sonido como el grito de los pavos reales; (4) el sonido *gandhāra*, sonido como el balido de las cabras; (5) […] sonido como el grito de las grullas; (6) el sonido *pañcama*, como el canto del cuco; (7) el sonido *nisāda*, sonido como el bramido de los elefantes: así hay (7), (o) 7 clases. Entre ellos, los músicos a veces encabezan e inician con el sonido *chajja* y, tras cantarlo y tocarlo, cantan y tocan los 6 sonidos restantes. A veces encabezan e inician con el sonido *majjhima* y, tras cantarlo y tocarlo, cantan y tocan los 6 sonidos restantes. A veces encabezan e inician con el sonido *gandhāra* y, tras cantarlo y tocarlo, cantan y tocan los 6 sonidos restantes. Entre ellos, a los (7) sonidos *chajja*, *usabha*, *gandhāra*, *majjhima*, *pañcama*, *dhevata*, *nisāda*, encabezados e iniciados por el sonido *chajja*, se les llama «*chajjagāma*, la serie de sonidos encabezada por el sonido *chajja*». A los (7) encabezados e iniciados por el sonido *majjhima* se les llama «*majjhimagāma*, la serie de sonidos encabezada por el sonido *majjhima*». A los 7 sonidos *gandhāra*, *majjhima*, *pañcama*, *dhevata*, *nisāda*, *chajja*, *usabha*, encabezados e iniciados por el sonido *gandhāra*, se les llama «*gandhāragāma*, la serie de sonidos encabezada por el sonido *gandhāra*». Por las 7 clases de sonidos del *chajjagāma*, las 7 clases […] y las 7 clases de sonidos del *gandhāragāma* ya mencionadas, los sonidos cantados y tocados son de 21 clases. El emitir los sonidos en grave y agudo para que surjan esas 21 clases de sonidos cantados y tocados (el cantar y tocar, *mucchanā*) se divide también en 21 clases. Por eso hay en total 21 clases de *mucchanā*. Otra explicación: el modo particular de cantar y tocar que llega a ser uno de los seis *rāga* cautivadores llamados *sirīrāga*, *vasanta*, *pañcama*, *bherava*, *megha*, *nāṭanārāyana* se llama *mucchanā*. Ese *mucchanā* es de 21 clases en total: 7 en el *chajjagāma*, llamados *lalitā*, *majjhimā*, *citrā*, *rohinī*, *mātaṅgajā*, *sovīrī*, *saṇḍamajjhā*; 7 en el *majjhimagāma*, llamados *pañcamā*, *maccharī*, *mudumajjhā*, *suddhā*, *antā*, *kalāvatī*, *tibbā*; 7 en el *gandhāragāma*, llamados *ruddī*, *brahmī*, *vesaṇavī*, *sedarī*, *surā*, *nādāvatī*, *visālā*. Pero en la exposición del *sakkapañhasutta* se dice que, según el modo de tocar del mundo humano, haciendo tres *mucchanā* en cada uno de los siete sonidos *chajja*, *usabha*, *gandhāra*, *majjhima*, *pañcama*, *dhevata*, *nisāda*, hay 21 *mucchanā*; según el modo de tocar del mundo de los *deva*, haciendo siete *mucchanā* en cada sonido, hay (49) *mucchanā*; y que en esos (49), el sonido intermedio llamado *antarasara* […].)
en: the fainting / the being stupefied; the emitting of the sounds low and high / the singing and playing. See also [[mucchana]]. (The sounds that are sung and played are: (1) the *usabha* sound, a sound like the lowing of oxen; (2) the *dhevata* sound, a sound like the neighing of horses; (3) the *chajja* sound, a sound like the cry of peacocks; (4) the *gandhāra* sound, a sound like the bleating of goats; (5) […] a sound like the call of cranes; (6) the *pañcama* sound, like the call of the cuckoo; (7) the *nisāda* sound, a sound like the trumpeting of elephants: thus there are (7), (or) 7 kinds. Among these, musicians sometimes lead off and begin with the *chajja* sound and, after singing and playing it, sing and play the remaining 6 sounds. Sometimes they lead off and begin with the *majjhima* sound and, after singing and playing it, sing and play the remaining 6 sounds. Sometimes they lead off and begin with the *gandhāra* sound and, after singing and playing it, sing and play the remaining 6 sounds. Among these, the (7) sounds *chajja*, *usabha*, *gandhāra*, *majjhima*, *pañcama*, *dhevata*, *nisāda*, led off and begun by the *chajja* sound, are called '*chajjagāma*, the series of sounds headed by the *chajja* sound'. The (7) led off and begun by the *majjhima* sound are called '*majjhimagāma*, the series of sounds headed by the *majjhima* sound'. The 7 sounds *gandhāra*, *majjhima*, *pañcama*, *dhevata*, *nisāda*, *chajja*, *usabha*, led off and begun by the *gandhāra* sound, are called '*gandhāragāma*, the series of sounds headed by the *gandhāra* sound'. By the 7 kinds of *chajjagāma* sounds, the 7 kinds […] and the 7 kinds of *gandhāragāma* sounds just mentioned, the sung and played sounds are of 21 kinds. The emitting of the sounds low and high so that those 21 kinds of sung and played sounds arise (singing and playing, *mucchanā*) is likewise divided into 21 kinds. Therefore there are 21 kinds of *mucchanā* in all. Another explanation: the particular way of singing and playing that attains the state of the six captivating *rāga* called *sirīrāga*, *vasanta*, *pañcama*, *bherava*, *megha*, *nāṭanārāyana* is called *mucchanā*. That *mucchanā* is of 21 kinds in all: 7 in the *chajjagāma*, called *lalitā*, *majjhimā*, *citrā*, *rohinī*, *mātaṅgajā*, *sovīrī*, *saṇḍamajjhā*; 7 in the *majjhimagāma*, called *pañcamā*, *maccharī*, *mudumajjhā*, *suddhā*, *antā*, *kalāvatī*, *tibbā*; 7 in the *gandhāragāma*, called *ruddī*, *brahmī*, *vesaṇavī*, *sedarī*, *surā*, *nādāvatī*, *visālā*. But in the exposition of the *sakkapañhasutta* it is said that, by the manner of playing of the human world, making three *mucchanā* on each of the seven sounds *chajja*, *usabha*, *gandhāra*, *majjhima*, *pañcama*, *dhevata*, *nisāda*, there are 21 *mucchanā*; by the manner of playing of the world of the *deva*, making seven *mucchanā* on each sound, there are (49) *mucchanā*; and that in those (49), the intermediate sound called *antarasara* […].)

en: *saṁyuttanikāya*; the collection of suttas in which the suttas beginning with the *oghataraṇa* and the vaggas beginning with the *naḷavagga* are joined together. The *saṁyuttanikāya* has, by vaggas, five vaggas: (1) *sagāthāvagga*, (2) *nidānavagga*, (3) *khandhavagga*, (4) *sal̤āyatanavagga*, (5) *mahāvagga*. Of these, in (1) the *sagāthāvagga* there are 13 saṁyuttas: (1) *devatāsaṁyutta*, (2) *devaputtasaṁyutta*, (3) *kosalasaṁyutta*, (4) *mārasaṁyutta*, (5) *bhikkhunīsaṁyutta*, (6) *brahmasaṁyutta*, (7) *brāhmaṇasaṁyutta*, (8) *vaṅgīsasaṁyutta*, (9) *vanasaṁyutta*, (10) *yakkhasaṁyutta*, (11) *sakkasaṁyutta*. Of these, in the *devatāsaṁyutta*: (1) *nal̤avagga* (10 suttas), (2) *nandanavagga* (10 suttas), (3) *sattivagga* (10 suttas), (4) *satullapakāyikavagga* (10 suttas), (5) *ādittavagga* (10 suttas), (6) *jarāvagga* (10 suttas), (7) *addhavagga* (10 suttas), (8) *chetvāvagga* (11 suttas); thus there are 8 inner vaggas and 81 suttas. In the *devaputtasaṁyutta*: (1) *paṭhamavagga* (10 suttas), (2) *anāthapiṇḍikavagga* (10 suttas), (3) *nānātitthiyavagga* (10 suttas); thus there are 3 inner vaggas and 30 suttas. In the *kosalasaṁyutta*: (1) *paṭhamavagga* (10 suttas), (2) *dutiyavagga* (10 suttas), (3) *tatiyavagga* (5 suttas); thus there are 3 inner vaggas and 25 suttas. In the *mārasaṁyutta*: (1) *paṭhamavagga* (10 suttas), (2) *dutiyavagga* (10 suttas), (3) *tatiyavagga* (5 suttas); thus there are 3 inner vaggas and 25 suttas. In the *bhikkhunīsaṁyutta* there is only one inner vagga, with 10 suttas. In the *brahmasaṁyutta*: (1) *paṭhamavagga* (10 suttas), *dutiyavagga* (5 suttas); thus there are 2 inner vaggas and 15 suttas. In the *brāhmaṇasaṁyutta*: (1) *arahantavagga* (10 suttas), (2) *upāsakavagga* (12 suttas); thus there are 2 inner vaggas and 22 suttas. es: el libro del comentario del *saṁyuttanikāya*; el libro del comentario del *saṁyutta*; el libro llamado *sāratthappakāsinī*; libro en que / por el cual se explica el significado del texto canónico del *saṁyuttanikāya*. (Este comentario lo expusieron y enseñaron, ya en vida del Buddha, tanto el propio Buddha como los *ariya*, sus discípulos, que comienzan por los *aggasāvaka*. Ese comentario lo recitaron en concilio, en el primer concilio, los 500 venerables *arahant* que comienzan por el venerable *thera* *mahākassapa*; en el segundo concilio, los 700 venerables *arahant* que comienzan por el venerable *thera* *yasa*; y en el tercer concilio, los 1000 venerables *arahant* que comienzan por el venerable *thera* *mahāmoggaliputtatissa*. El *thera* *mahinda*, discípulo corresidente del venerable *thera* *moggaliputtatissa* e hijo del gran rey *asoka*, llevó ese comentario del *saṁyutta* desde la isla de *jambudīpa* a la isla de *sīhaḷa* (*sirilaṅkā*) y lo dejó en lengua cingalesa para beneficio de los monjes de la isla. Después, el venerable *thera* *mahābuddhaghosa* lo tradujo del cingalés a la lengua *māgadha* y lo puso por escrito.)
en: the book of the commentary on the *saṁyuttanikāya*; the book of the commentary on the *saṁyutta*; the book named *sāratthappakāsinī*; the book in which / by which the meaning of the canonical text of the *saṁyuttanikāya* is explained. (This commentary was expounded and taught already in the Buddha's lifetime both by the Buddha himself and by the *ariya*, his disciples, beginning with the *aggasāvaka*. That commentary was recited in council: at the first council by the 500 venerable *arahant* beginning with the venerable *thera* *mahākassapa*; at the second council by the 700 venerable *arahant* beginning with the venerable *thera* *yasa*; and at the third council by the 1000 venerable *arahant* beginning with the venerable *thera* *mahāmoggaliputtatissa*. The *thera* *mahinda*, co-resident pupil of the venerable *thera* *moggaliputtatissa* and son of the great king *asoka*, brought that commentary on the *saṁyutta* from the island of *jambudīpa* to the island of *sīhaḷa* (*sirilaṅkā*) and set it down in Sinhalese for the benefit of the monks of the island. Afterwards the venerable *thera* *mahābuddhaghosa* translated it from Sinhalese into the *māgadha* language and wrote it down.)

es: (1) el cerrar / impedir / obstruir. (2) el contener / guardar. (3) el no transgredir. (4) el prohibir. (5) los cinco estados que suelen cerrar / impedir / obstruir / prohibir, o que son causa de ello (…, conocimiento, …). (6) *paccayapaṭisevanā*. (7) *ājīvapārisuddhi*. (8) que suele cerrar / impedir / obstruir / prohibir (dicho de una persona). (9) el límite / la regla que es el medio / la causa de la contención. (10) (por metonimia del fruto) los nueve estados de *saṁvara*: (a) *subharatā* (el hecho de ser mantenido con facilidad). (b) *suposatā* (el hecho de ser mantenido con facilidad). (c) *appiccha* (el tener pocos deseos). (d) *santuṭṭha* (el contentarse). (e) *sallekha* (el hacer menguar las *kilesa*). (f) *dhuta* (el sacudirse las *kilesa*). (g) *pāsādika* (el suscitar lo que inspira devoción). (h) *apacaya* (el destruir todas las *kilesa*). (i) *vīriyārambha* (el emprender el esfuerzo). (11) el rey / príncipe llamado *saṁvara*. (12) el sutta *saṁvara*. (13) el jātaka *saṁvara*. (14) el señor de los *asura* llamado *saṁvara*.
en: (1) the closing / blocking / obstructing. (2) the restraining / guarding. (3) the not transgressing. (4) the prohibiting. (5) the five states that are apt to close / block / obstruct / prohibit, or are the cause of it (…, knowledge, …). (6) *paccayapaṭisevanā*. (7) *ājīvapārisuddhi*. (8) apt to close / block / obstruct / prohibit (said of a person). (9) the limit / rule that is the means / cause of restraint. (10) (by metonymy of the fruit) the nine states of *saṁvara*: (a) *subharatā* (the state of being easily supported). (b) *suposatā* (the state of being easily supported). (c) *appiccha* (having few wishes). (d) *santuṭṭha* (being content). (e) *sallekha* (wearing down the *kilesa*). (f) *dhuta* (shaking off the *kilesa*). (g) *pāsādika* (bringing about what inspires devotion). (h) *apacaya* (destroying all the *kilesa*). (i) *vīriyārambha* (undertaking effort). (11) the king / prince named *saṁvara*. (12) the *saṁvara* sutta. (13) the *saṁvara* jātaka. (14) the lord of the *asura* named *saṁvara*.
